title: Semantic structure and accessible names
learningObjectives: Explain semantic structure and accessible names and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: Semantic HTML elements communicate purpose and structure. Accessible names identify controls to assistive technologies and can come from associated labels, visible text, or ARIA naming attributes. Landmarks such as header, nav, main, and footer support navigation.
understand.whyItMatters: Semantic structure improves keyboard and assistive-technology navigation and makes documents easier to understand. Generic div elements require extra work to recreate native meaning.
understand.analogy: Semantic elements are signposts that tell visitors and assistive tools what each area is for.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The elements identify page landmarks and headings; the navigation landmark has an accessible name.

examples.explanation: The elements identify page landmarks and headings; the navigation landmark has an accessible name.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the concept; some browser examples require a real served page and supported APIs.

practise.guidedTask: Replace generic containers in a sample page with appropriate landmarks and label every form control.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
hints: Use browser developer tools to inspect actual behaviour.
Test with keyboard and different viewport sizes.
Keep core content available when enhancements are unsupported.
